items.title: PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3 : Major Security Update
items.summary: Eymoutiers, France, October 27th, 2026Dalibo is pleased to announce PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3 with a panel ofimportant security fixes.Enhanced Privacy Protection for Your DataPostgreSQL Anonymizer is an extension that hides or replaces personallyidentifiable information (PII) or commercially sensitive data from a PostgreSQLdatabase.The extension offers 6 different masking strategies:Dynamic Masking - Real-time data protectionStatic Masking - Permanent data transformationReplica Masking - Anonymized logical replicationBackup Masking - Privacy-protected database exportsMasking Views - Controlled data visibilityMasking Data Wrappers - Extended protection across systemsEach strategy is complemented by an enhanced suite of Masking Functions, includingadvanced techniques such as: Substitution, Randomization, Faking, Pseudonymization,Partial Scrambling, Shuffling, Noise Addition and Generalization.The extension can be installed with Debian and RPM packages, an Ansible role, a Dockerimage, etc. You can use it on most major DBaaS providers including : Alibaba Cloud,Crunchy Bridge, Google Cloud SQL, IBM Cloud, Microsoft Azure Database, Neon, YandexIt is also available on some Postgres forks such as EDB Advanced Postgres, Greenplumand Yugabyte.See the INSTALL section of the documentation for more details!Important Security UpdateVersion 3.3 includes fixes for 12 critical vulnerabilities allowing some users to gain superuser privileges under certain circumstances or allowing maskedusers to access personal information.These vulnerabilities are declared below:CVE-2026-110181: Masked roles read the authentic data through SQL functions  with a SQL-standard bodyCVE-2026-105615: Masked roles can read pg_statsCVE-2026-105616: The secret salt is readable in pg_db_role_settingCVE-2026-110183: After the static masking, pg_stats keeps the authentic  values of the masked columnsCVE-2026-105619: Masking rules are not applied through security_invoker  viewsCVE-2026-105618: Dynamic masking does not work on inherited tablesCVE-2026-110182: anon.partial() and anon.partial_email() can leak dataCVE-2026-105617: Cached plans bypass transparent dynamic maskingCVE-2026-105620: Unauthorized access via subqueriesCVE-2026-105612: Data-modifying CTEs bypass the read-only restrictionCVE-2026-105614: Unbounded memory allocation (DoS) in image functionsCVE-2026-105613: DoS in range-based dummy functionsAll users should upgrade the extension to version 3.3 as soon as possible.UpgradeVersion 3.3 brings a series of new restrictions to prevent malicious behaviours.Subqueries in masking rules are now forbiddenInlining of functions is disabled for transparent dynamic maskingWith dynamic masking, masked role are forbidden from  executing function with SQL-standard bodies. This includes functions in  contrib extensions that use this form (citext, earthdistance, etc. )It is also strongly advised to change the value of the anon.salt GUC parameter.See the UPGRADE section for more details.AcknowledgmentsThis release includes code, bugfixes, documentation, code reviews and ideasfrom Alain Lesage, @dmeremyanin, Gregoire Hubert and other contributors.Kudos to @dmeremyanin for his first contributions !The security issues were reported by Alexander Kukushkin and Ilya Staroverov.Many thanks to them for their efforts, their availability and the quality oftheir work.And also special thanks to the PGRX team for their amazing work!Join our community to improve data privacy!PostgreSQL Anonymizer is part of the [Dalibo Labs] initiative. It is mainlydeveloped by [Damien Clochard] and [Benoit Lobréau].This is an open project, contributions are welcome. We need your feedback andideas! Let us know what you think of this tool, how it fits your needs andwhat features are missing.If you want to help, you can find a list of Junior Jobs.
